fields.apa_citation: Siniscalco, A., & Bortolotti, A. (2024). Physiology and psychology of light and colour: Evaluation of an experimental approach. [Conference paper, exact venue/year and page range not printed in the retrieved text; hosted on ResearchGate, publication ID 376553234].
fields.main_conclusion: Evaluating how light and colour affect human psychology and physiology in a way useful for lighting design requires a carefully staged experimental approach -- beginning with controlled, single-colour presentation (e.g., via a calibrated VR display) and progressing to naturalistic, dynamically lit mock-up environments -- because prior colour-emotion research suffers from poor colour control, neglect of environmental factors, and underpowered samples.
independent_variables: Colour/light stimulus (hue, spectral power distribution) -- proposed, not tested
Luminous intensity / correlated colour temperature -- proposed, not tested
dependent_variables: Psychological/emotional response to colour -- proposed, not tested
Physiological arousal (e.g., melatonin suppression, heart rate/activation) -- proposed, not tested
fields.construct_pair: Light/colour exposure -> Psychological and physiological response
fields.stimulus_description: No stimulus was administered; the paper proposes future presentation of defined colours via an appropriately calibrated screen or VR headset at a fixed focal distance, followed by a second series of tests in a mock-up living environment illuminated by a dynamic coloured-lighting system.
fields.methods_surface_summary: This is a position/theoretical paper, not an empirical study: it reviews the Ecological Valence Theory and Color-in-Context Theory, catalogues methodological pitfalls in colour-emotion research, and outlines a proposed two-stage experimental design (controlled VR/screen colour exposure, then a naturalistic dynamically-lit room) for future testing.
